n: The heading places this when the Philistines seized David in Gath. He asks for mercy because enemies keep trampling him day after day.

f.g: Trample or pant after me, eager to destroy.

n: Many proud enemies attack him every day. He appeals to God Most High.

f.g: Possibly “proudly” — describing how the enemies fight.

n: A short, honest verse: when I’m afraid, I choose to trust you. Faith doesn’t mean never feeling fear; it means what we do with it.
Here is the refrain (repeated in verses 10–11): trusting God’s word, he won’t fear what mere mortals can do.

f.w: I will not fear what flesh can do unto me

n: All day they twist his words and think up ways to hurt him.
They band together, lurk in hiding, and watch his every step, waiting to take his life.

f.g: Watch my heels — track my movements.

n: Will they get away with their evil? David asks God to bring down such nations in his anger.
A beautiful image: God has counted every one of David’s restless wanderings and kept every tear in a bottle. Not one sorrow is forgotten or wasted.

f.w: put thou my tears into thy bottle
f.g: A leather or clay container — God treasures each tear.

f.w: are they not in thy book?

n: When he calls, his enemies will retreat. He is sure of one thing: God is on his side.
The refrain returns with both names: in God and in the LORD he praises the word of promise.
Trust replaces fear: what can any human do to him?

f.w: I will not be afraid what man can do unto me

n: David feels bound by the vows he made to God and will keep them by offering thanks.

f.g: I am obligated by the promises I made to you.

n: God has rescued him from death and kept his feet from stumbling, so he can walk before God in the light of life.
